Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:10:1.hebrew: דומיא דיין - דסמוך ליה: "ויין לא ישתו בבואם" וגו' — מקיש פרועי ראש לשתויי יין, וכתיב ביין: "בבואם":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:10:1.english: Similar to wine - For juxtaposed to it [is]: "Neither shall they drink wine when they enter," etc. [Scripture thereby] compares those with overgrown hair to those who drink wine, and regarding wine it is written: "When they enter."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:1.hebrew: רבי אומר אומר אני כהן אסור לשתות יין לעולם - רישא דברייתא קתני: כהן המכיר משמרתו ומשמרת בית אב שלו — אסור ביין כל אותו היום, אף בזמן הזה. מכיר משמרתו ואינו מכיר בית אב שלו — אסור כל אותו שבת. אינו מכיר לא משמרתו ולא משמרת בית אב שלו — אסור לשתות יין לעולם, שמא עכשיו זמנו הוא, ויש לחוש שמא יבנה בית המקדש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:1.english: Rabbi says: I say, a priest is forbidden to drink wine forever - The first clause of the *baraita* teaches: A priest who knows his [priestly] watch and the watch of his ancestral house is forbidden [to drink] wine that entire day, even nowadays. [If he] knows his [priestly] watch but does not know his ancestral house, he is forbidden [wine] that entire week. [If he] knows neither his [priestly] watch nor the watch of his ancestral house, he is forbidden to drink wine forever, lest now is his time [to serve], and there is concern lest the Temple be rebuilt.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:2.hebrew: רבי אומר אומר אני - אם באנו לחוש שמא יבנה, אסור ביין לעולם, ואפילו הוא מכיר שאינו עכשיו זמן משמרתו — שמא יבנה, וכל הקודם ואישתכח עייל ועביד:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:2.english: Rabbi says: I say - If we are to be concerned that [the Temple] might be rebuilt, [a priest] is forbidden [to drink] wine forever, and even if he knows that it is not now the time of his priestly watch — lest it be rebuilt, and whoever is first and present enters and performs [the service].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:3.hebrew: אבל מה אעשה שתקנתן קלקלתן - חורבן הבית שקלקלן ועירבב סדר' משמרותיהן — שהיה אוסרן ביין בזמן משמרתן ומתירן שלא בזמן משמרתן — הוא תיקנן עכשיו לשתות יין לעולם, דלא חייש שמא יבנה פתאום:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:3.english: But what can I do, as their repair is their ruin - The destruction of the Temple, which ruined them and disrupted the order of their priestly watches — which used to prohibit them from [drinking] wine during the time of their watch and permit them when not during the time of their watch — it “repaired” them now [by allowing them] to drink wine always, as [Rabbi] is not concerned lest [the Temple] be rebuilt suddenly.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:4.hebrew: כמאן שתו האידנא כהני חמרא כרבי - שהרי רוב כהנים אינן בקיאין בזמן משמרותיהן, ואסורין לעולם לרבנן:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:11:4.english: In accordance with whom do priests drink wine nowadays? In accordance with Rabbi - For most priests are not familiar with the time of their [priestly] watches, and [therefore] are forbidden forever according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:12:1.hebrew: התם היינו טעמא כו' - שינויא היא, ובניחותא גרסינן לה. כלומר: מדאוריי' שרי, ורבנן הוא דגזור:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:12:1.english: There, this is the reason, etc. - It is an answer, and we read it calmly [as a statement]. That is to say: by Torah law it is permitted, and it was the Rabbis who decreed [it].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:12:2.hebrew: ופרכינן: הכא נמי מהרה יבנה וכו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:12:2.english: And we object: Here too, [the Temple will] speedily be built, etc.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:14:1.hebrew: שתויי יין דמחלי עבודה - דכתיב (ויקרא י׳:י׳) יין ושכר וגו', וסמיך: "ולהבדיל בין הקדש ובין החול", משמע: בין עבודה קדושה לעבודה מחוללת. גזרו בהו רבנן בזמן הזה — משום "מהרה יבנה":
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:14:1.english: [Priests] drunk on wine, who desecrate the service - As it is written (Leviticus 10:10): "Wine and strong drink..." and adjacent [to it is]: "And to distinguish between the holy and the common" — meaning, between sacred service and desecrated service. The Sages decreed regarding them in the present era [not to drink], due to [the concern that the Temple] may speedily be rebuilt:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:18:1.hebrew: ה"ג - אף פרועי ראש מחלי עבודה, קשיא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:18:1.english: This is the reading: Even priests with long hair desecrate the Temple service; [this poses] a difficulty.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:1.english: This, until Ezekiel came - And juxtaposed them.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:2.hebrew: מאן אמרה - פירוש: מהיכא נפקא לן פרועי ראש במיתה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:2.english: Who said it? - Meaning: From where do we derive that [priests with] overgrown hair [are liable to] death?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:3.hebrew: הא דאמר רב חסדא - בזבחים, בפ' שני. "דבר זה" — דכהן ערל פסול לעבודה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:3.english: This [statement] that Rav Ḥisda said - [It is found] in Zevachim, in the second chapter. “This matter” — that an uncircumcised priest is disqualified from [Temple] service.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:4.hebrew: כל בן נכר - כהן שנתנכרו מעשיו לאביו שבשמים ונערל לבו, או ערל בשר שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:19:4.english: Any stranger - A priest whose deeds have become estranged from his Father in Heaven and whose heart has become uncircumcised; or [a priest who is] uncircumcised in flesh, whose brothers died due to circumcision.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:21:1.english: Unique - Handsome, and there is nothing like it.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:22:1.hebrew: בן אלעשה - חתנו של רבי היה, ונתן ממון ולמדו לו אותה תספורת:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:22:1.english: Ben Elasa - He was the son-in-law of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and he gave money and they learned that haircut for him.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:2:1.english: She lets [it] pass with a word - She overlooks offenses.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:3:1.english: She is raw material - Before she has had intercourse.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:3:2.hebrew: גולם - כלי שלא נגמר קרוי גולם, כדתנן: גולמי כלי עץ טמאין:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:3:2.english: Raw material - A vessel that has not been finished is called a golem, as we learned in a Mishnah: "Unfinished wooden vessels are [susceptible to] ritual impurity."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:6:1.hebrew: משמרות - מתחלפות ומתחדשות בשבת — זו יוצאה וזו נכנסת — וצריך להסתפר מפני משמרת חדשה זו הנכנסת, שיראוהו ביופי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:6:1.english: [The priestly] watches - They rotate and are renewed on Shabbat — this [one] departs and this [one] enters — and [the High Priest] must have his hair cut on account of this incoming new watch, so that they will see him in [his] beauty.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:9:1.hebrew: לא לירבו כלל - ואפי' עד שלשים:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:9:1.english: They should not grow [their hair] at all - And even up to thirty [days].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:9:2.english: [Abaye] said to him - [Hair] is called pera at thirty days.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:9:3.hebrew: אי הוה כתיב לא ישלחו פרע - הוה משמע: לא יגדלו פרע עד שיעור פרע. השתא דכתיב "ופרע לא ישלחו", דקאמר "פרע" והדר "לא ישלחו" — משמע: פרע דשלשים יום ליהוי, אבל שלוחי טפי לא לשלחו:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 22b:9:3.english: Had it been written: “They shall not grow long hair” - It would have implied: They shall not grow hair up to the measure of long hair [thirty days]. Now that it is written: “And long hair they shall not grow,” as it states “long hair” and then “they shall not grow,” it implies: Let there be long hair of thirty days, but they shall not let it grow out more [than that].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:19:1.hebrew: אלא גמרא גמירי לה ואתא יחזקאל ואסמכה אקרא - וקשה: הרי רב אשי עצמו סותר דבריו, ומיישב הך הקישא דיחזקאל שסותר דבריו הראשונים — דאמר רב אשי לעיל: "פרועי ראש דלא מחלי עבודה"?! וי"ל: ממה שרב אשי אמר "גמרא גמירי ואתא יחזקאל ואסמכה אקרא", מתרצי שתי הקושיות: ד"עד דאתי יחזקאל מאן אמרה", ומתרצה קושיא דלעיל. דכיון דגמרא היא, מצינו למימר: הכי גמירי הלכתא — למיתה, ואחולי עבודה לא גמירי; ויחזקאל אסמכה אקרא — מענין ההלכה אסמכה, וא"כ לא אסמכינן לעשות ההקישא רק לענין מיתה. אבל לעיל, דלא ידע דגמיר הלכה, סבר הוא לעשות הקישא מפרועי ראש לשתויי יין מכל וכל, דאין היקש למחצה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:19:1.english: "Rather, it is learned as a tradition, and Ezekiel came and supported it with a verse" - And [this is] difficult: For doesn't Rav Ashi himself contradict his own words, by resolving this juxtaposition in Ezekiel that contradicts his earlier words, as Rav Ashi said above: "[Priests with] long hair do not desecrate the service"?! And it can be said: From what Rav Ashi said, "It is learned as a tradition, and Ezekiel came and supported it with a verse," both difficulties are resolved: [that of] "Until Ezekiel came, who said it?", and the difficulty from above is [also] resolved. For since it is a tradition, we can say: Thus was the halakha learned — regarding death; but regarding desecrating the service, it was not learned. And when Ezekiel supported it with a verse, he supported it in accordance with the subject matter of the halakha; and if so, we do not anchor [it] to make the juxtaposition except regarding the matter of death. But above, when [the questioner] did not know that it was a learned halakha, he thought to make a juxtaposition between [priests with] long hair and [priests] drunk on wine in every respect, for there is no partial juxtaposition.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:21:1.hebrew: כסום יכסמו - פי': כעין כוסמת, הגדל כך שבלין — ראשו של זה בצד עיקרו של זה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:21:1.english: “They shall surely trim” - Explanation: [The term is] like spelt [kusemet], which grows with its ears [arranged] like this — the top of this [one] alongside the base of that [one].

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:9:1.hebrew: ואימא לא לירבו כלל - תימה: ד"פרע" — "פרע" במאי מוקי לה? אלא נראה לומר דה"פ: אימא לא לירבו שלשים, דהיינו שיעור פרע, אלא יגלחו בכ"ט. ומשני: אי כתיב "לא ישלחו פרע", משמע: לא ישלחו שיעור פרע; אבל השתא דכתיב "פרע" קמא — "לא ישלחו" משמע: טפי מפרע לא ישלחו:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 22b:9:1.english: "And say that they should not grow [hair] at all" - [This is] puzzling: for [the word] "pera" — how does he interpret "pera"? Rather, it seems that this is its explanation: Say that they should not grow [hair for] thirty [days], which is the measure of pera, but rather they must cut [their hair] on the twenty-ninth [day]. And [Abaye] answers: Had it been written: "They shall not let grow long hair [pera]," it would imply: they shall not let [it] reach the measure of pera; but now that "pera" is written first — "they shall not let grow" implies: more than pera they shall not let grow.
